c--c-data-structures--draft.title: Data Structures in C
c--c-data-structures--draft.description: A trace-first C algorithms course built from CS260 Written Assignment 2: every concept is explained with concrete values, data or call-tree animation, correctness reasoning, runtime analysis, and hands-on implementation.
c--c-data-structures--draft.moreComingSoon: Later modules can add linked structures, graph traversal, sorting, and deeper asymptotic analysis.

c--c-data-structures--draft-module-1-alg.title: Algorithm Design Lab
c--c-data-structures--draft-module-1-alg.description: Work through recursion, pair sums, BST construction/rebalancing, stack-only priority queues, and pointer heaps with board-style step-by-step traces. Recursive procedures are always visualized as call trees.
outcomes: Connect a recursive call tree to a recurrence and a tight asymptotic bound.
Use bounded pair sums to detect equal-sum disjoint pairs in quadratic time.
Build and rebuild almost-balanced binary search trees in linear time.
Implement a priority queue using only legal stack operations.
Insert into a pointer-based complete heap by following the binary path of the next index.
why: Concrete function traces make pointer changes, recursive control flow, and loop invariants visible before learners write code.
Behavioral tests reward correct algorithms instead of brittle source phrases, formatting, helper names, or one canonical implementation.

c--c-data-structures--draft-algorithm-de.title: From Written Algorithms to Working C
c--c-data-structures--draft-algorithm-de.description: Each problem moves from contract to concrete trace, structure animation, correctness argument, runtime derivation, and hands-on C implementation.
bullets: O(log n) insertion in a pointer-based heap
